lines.text: An attribute for defining the height of lines in a text.
- Important: Note that this attribute is not for usage with CoreText
APIs directly, but exposed to give other frameworks common vocabulary to
express the line height concept as defined by CoreText in Swift. For
more details, see ``Foundation/AttributeScopes/CoreTextAttributes``.
The line height definition of a paragraph.
The line height defines the distance between the baselines of two
subsequent lines of text.
Returns a Boolean value indicating whether two values are not equal.
Inequality is the inverse of equality. For any values `a` and `b`, `a != b`
implies that `a == b` is `false`.
This is the default implementation of the not-equal-to operator (`!=`)
for any type that conforms to `Equatable`.
- Parameters:
- lhs: A value to compare.
- rhs: Another value to compare.
Variable line height based on font metrics.
Defines the line height based on the ascent and descent of the
fonts used in each line.
Constant line height based on a multiple of the point size that is
perceived as normal.
Constant line height based on a multiple of the point size that is
perceived as tight.
Constant line height based on a multiple of the point size that is
perceived as loose.
Constant line height based on a multiple of the point size.
Definines the line height based on the largest point size multiplied
by `factor`, regardless of the effective ascent and descent of the
fonts in use.
Constant line height based on point size and a fixed increase.
Defines the line height based on the largest point size plus an
`increase` (in points), regardless of the effective ascent and
descent of the fonts in use.
Constant line height based on a fixed total.
Defines the line height as the exact given total (in points),
regardless of the effective ascent and descent of the fonts in use.

A namespace for attributes defined by CoreText.
Note that this is _not_ an
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Foundation/AttributeScope>,
but merely a namespace for
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Foundation/AttributedStringKey>s
that describe CoreText concepts. Those attributes may be used by _other
frameworks_ to describe those concepts. Unless documented otherwise,
frameworks generally inidcate support for a certain attribute by adding
it to the framework's
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Foundation/AttributeScope>.
CoreText specifically does not support Swift
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Foundation/AttributedStringKey>,
and will not recognize the attributes nested in this namespace when used
directly with CoreText API, no matter if used in an `AttributedString`
or `NSAttributedString`.
An attribute defining the explicit horizontal alignment of a paragraph.
- Important: Note that this attribute is not for usage with CoreText
APIs directly, but exposed to give other frameworks common vocabulary to
express the text alignment concept as defined by CoreText in Swift. For
more details, see ``Foundation/AttributeScopes/CoreTextAttributes``.
The explicit alignment of text within its container.
Alignment defines the horizontal position of each line within its
container.
